texts.preamble: State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 In The Court Of Shri Sanjay Sharma-I Addl. Sessions Judge - 01 (North-East) Karkardooma Courts : Delhi Sc No. 44715/2015 Fir No. 17/2014 Ps Bhajanpura Under Section 354-A/354-D Ipc & 8/12 Pocso Act State Versus Fareed Ahmed S/o Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, R/o B-674/2, Gali No.7, Subhash Vihar, North Ghonda, Delhi. Date of institution of case : 26.02.2014 Date on which judgment reserved : 15.12.2016 Date of judgment pronounced : 20.12.2016 Judgment:
texts.facts: 1. On 04.01.2014, on receipt of DD No.77-B, SI Yogesh Kumar of PS Bhajanpura reached the spot i.e. a cylinder shop in Gali No. 5, Subhash Mohalla, Bhajanpura, Delhi where he came to know that the complainant and the accused had already been taken to the police station by the PCR officials. Accordingly, he returned to the PS where the vicitm, a minor girl, aged about 17 years met him and gave a written complaint to him, addressed to the SHO alleging that "she used to go to Shani Bazaar at Ghonda every Saturday to purchase vegetables. For the last three-four weeks, one boy had been meeting her in the market and used to tease her. The boy used to ask her to have friendship with him and used to follow her from the market to her house. She had informed about it to her parents. Despite her persistent requests, he did not mend his ways. On 04.01.2014, her brother Neeraj gave her assurance and asked her that she need not fear from that boy and if the boy again repeats his acts, she should inform him on phone. On that day, at about 07.00pm, when she had gone to market and was purchasing vegetables, the boy again came to her and asked her name and started teasing her and when she started to walk ahead, he caught her hand and teased her. She then raised an alarm. Some public persons rescued her from the boy and started beating him. Meanwhile, she called her brother SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 1 of 10 through phone who came there, caught the boy and made a call at number 100 and a PCR van arrived at the spot. She came to know the name of the said boy as Fareed Ahmad and also about his parentage and address". 2. On the basis of above complaint, a case was registered for the offences punishable under Section 354(A)(D) IPC and Section 8/12 of the POCSO Act. The accused was arrested. The victim was produced before the Ld. MM where her statement under Section 164 CrPC was recorded. After completion of investigation, chargesheet was filed against accused Fareed Ahmed for the said offences. State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/ 1 3. After hearing arguments on charge and considering the material on record, Ld. Predecessor framed a charge against the accused for the offences punishable under Section 8/12 of the POCSO Act and alternatively under Section 354-A/354-D IPC, dated 24.03.2014, to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. 4. In order to establish its case, the prosecution examined ten witnesses at the trial. 5. PW-1 Neeraj Kumar was the brother of the victim, who deposed about the incident. PW-2 HC Pramod Kumar Tiwari was the duty officer and had recorded the information regarding incident vide DD No.77-B, which he handed over to SI Yogesh Kumar for further proceedings. 6. PW-3 Ct. Mahesh Kumar was given the custody of the accused by SI Yogesh Kumar at the PS and was also a witness to the arrest proceedings of the accused. He also got the accused medically examined in the hospital. 7. PW-4 Sh. Ram Tek, Assistant Public Health Inspector, Shahdara, North Zone, EDMC, Delhi produced the birth certificate of the victim and proved it as Ex.PW4/A and deposed that as per the said certificate, the date of birth of the victim was 01.04.1996. 8. PW-5 lady Ct. Snehlata had received the call regarding the incident and proved the PCR form as Ex.PW5/A and a certificate under Section 65-B of the Evidence Act, issued by their nodal officer in respect of the said form, as Ex.PW5/B. SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 2 of 10 9 . PW-6 ASI Puran Singh had produced the call detail records of PCR van, Baker- 24 and proved it as Ex.PW6/A to Ex.PW6/C, respectively. PW-7 SI Ajay Pal Singh was the PCR van incharge and had reached the spot on receipt of information from the PCR Headquarter. 10. PW-8 Sh. Israr Babu, alternate Nodal Officer from Vodafone Mobile Services Ltd. proved the call detail records, collected during the course of investigation. PW- 9 was the victim herself, who deposed about the incident. PW-10 IO SI Yogesh Kumar deposed about the investigation conducted by him. 11. Statement of the accused was recorded under Section 313 CrPC wherein all the entire incriminating evidence was put to him which he denied and pleaded his innocence. He took the defence that he was falsely implicated in this case by the victim and her so-called brother with the connivance of the police. 12. In order to prove his innocence, the accused examined one witness in his defence i.e. DW-1 Sh. Hamid Khan. 13. I have heard Sh. Sukhbeer Singh - Ld. Addl. PP for the State, Sh. Sanjeev Shukla - Ld. Counsel for the accused and have gone through the records. State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/ 2 14. The main witness of this case was the victim herself whose version was corroborated by PW-1, her brother. It is observed that the victim has stood her ground and had maintained her version at every stage of the proceedings. She made categoric allegations in the FIR which were duly supported by her in her statement under Section 164 CrPC and then in her deposition before the Court. In her complaint on which the FIR was registered, she alleged that she used to go to purchase vegetables on every Saturday from the weekly market and a boy had been teasing her for the last three-four weeks. She stated that the said boy used to ask her for having friendship with him and followed her and did not mend his ways. She further stated that on 01.04.2014, her brother Neeraj gave her courage and also provided his mobile phone and asked her if the said boy again teases, she should call him. At about 07.00pm, when she was in the market, the said boy came to her, asked SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 3 of 10 her name and started teasing her and when she started to move from there he caught hold of her hand on which she raised an alarm, hearing which some public persons got her released and gave beatings to the accused. In the meanwhile, she called her brother who arrived there and called the PCR. 15. The victim gave almost similar statement to the Ld. MM under Section 164 CrPC which is Ex.PW9/B and in her statement before the Court, she made almost identical deposition. 16. She was duly cross-examined by the Ld. Defence Counsel. However, nothing material came out so as to disbelieve her version. In other words, her testimony could not be shaken in the cross-examination. She denied knowing any boy by the name of Gaurav or that said Gaurav was a friend of her brother Neeraj (PW-1). She admitted that name of her elder uncle (taau) was Sh. Radhey Shyam but could not say if he had lodged an FIR on 26.03.2013 against Gaurav having kidnapped her. She was given the suggestion, which was the defence of the accused, that she was recovered alongwith Gaurav at the behest of accused in December, 2013 and thereafter, she and the said Gaurav apprised Neeraj about it and they were annoyed of the acts of the accused and as such, Neeraj had given beatings to the accused in the market and thereafter, she conspired with Neeraj and implicated the accused in this case. She denied all these suggestions. She was also confronted with the copy of the said FIR which she admitted, but submitted further that the final report of the said FIR be also considered. State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/ 3 18. DW-1 never disclosed the name of the alleged two boys who were beating the accused and hence, the defence of the accused that it was Neeraj and Gaurav who had given beatings to the accused, could not be corroborated and substantiated. 20. The version of the victim was corroborated by PW-1, who deposed that the victim was just like his sister and had informed him through his wife that a boy had been teasing the victim for the last two-three Saturdays when she used to go to the market and used to follow her to her house. He further deposed that on 04.01.2014 at about 07.00/07.15pm, he received a phone call from the victim on his mobile phone, who disclosed him about the presence of the same boy and further told him that he was teasing her. Accordingly, he went there and found a crowd and the victim crying and accused was also present there who had been beaten by the public. Accordingly, he called the PCR. He also admitted the fact that the uncle of the victim, Sh. Radhey Shyam had lodged a missing report in respect of the victim at PS M.S. Park on 26.03.2013 but denied the suggestion that the victim had married with one Gaurav. He was confronted with his previous SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 5 of 10 statement Ex.PW1/BA wherein he had not stated that the victim had told his wife that accused used to tease her.
texts.arguments: 4. On the other hand, Ld. Counsel for the convict submitted that the convict is aged about 26 years. It was further submitted that he is unmarried and is working in DTC as a conductor on daily wages and that he has to look after his aged parents, younger brother and a younger marriageable sister. It was further submitted that the convict is a first time offender with no criminal antecedents nor is wanted in any other case of criminal nature. 7. In Daulat Ram Vs. State of Haryana AIR 1972 SC 2434, it was observed that Section 6 of Probation of Offender Act should be liberally construed so that its operation may be effective and beneficial to the young offenders who are prone more easily to be led astray by the influence of bad company. In Ishar Dass Vs. State of Punjab 1972 AIR 1295 SC, the appellant was convicted for the offence under Section 7 (1) of the Prevention of Food State vs Fareed Ahmed S/O Sh. Aneesh Ahmad, on 21 December, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135448572/ 6 Adulteration Act which carries a minimum sentence of imprisonment of six months, yet the the benefit of Probation SC No.44715/2015 - FIR No.17/2014 PS Bhajanpura page 9 of 10 of Offenders Act was extended to him.
